end.summary:
Practised showing that sums of consecutive odd numbers form square numbers using dot patterns and L-shapes.
Answered 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 correctly.
Identified that 16 is not odd.
The belief that adding odd numbers always gives an odd number remained at the final turn; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised square-number patterns with Saanvi by adding consecutive odd numbers and building squares with dot arrays and L-shapes. Saanvi correctly stated that 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 and noticed that 16 is not odd. They still mixed up the rule at the end, so it was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, draw successive squares and add the new L-shaped odd-number layer each time: 1, then 1 + 3, then 1 + 3 + 5.
